newsitem.title: FRANCE: Giscard says Bank of France has room to cut rates.
newsitem.headline: Giscard says Bank of France has room to cut rates.

text.p: Former French president Valery Giscard d'Estaing said in an interview published on Friday the Bank of France had room to cut interest rates as they were high for a country with inflation under control.

In an interview with financial daily La Tribune, Giscard d'Estaing also repeated his recent calls for a weaker franc against the dollar and said a level of 5.50 to 5.60 francs to the dollar should be the objective.
He said the planned single European currency should be worth two marks or seven francs which meant the franc/mark parity would be 3.50, compared with 3.3770 on Friday.
Giscard said Germany had a legitimate point of view on their economy and if the Bundesbank had decided there was no room for rate cuts France should not harbour any resentment.
However he said "As for me, I say France has room to cut interest rates."
He said the recent Bank of France rate cut was a move in the right direction and by lowering rates unilaterally it showed the central bank was not insensitive to calls for lower rates.
However he said the cut was "timid" and that "interest rates are still fairly high for a country where inflation is under control. We have to continue."
The former president also repeated his call for the creation of a special parliamentary committee to supervise the planned Euro currency to balance the power of the European central bank.
